extraction.name: MATH
extraction.description: MATH is a dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems designed to measure mathematical problem-solving ability in machine learning models. Each problem includes a full step-by-step solution to teach models to generate answer derivations and explanations.
extraction.creator: Dan Hendrycks, Collin Bums, Saurav Kadavath, Akul Arora, Steven Basart, Eric Tang, Dawn Song, Jacob Steinhardt
extraction.publisher: 35th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2021) Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by collecting high school math competition problems from the Art of Problem Solving (AoPS) website, pulling exercises from Khan Academy using open-source code, and algorithmically generating millions of synthetic problems using custom Mathematica scripts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of high school math competition problems (such as AMC 10, AMC 12, and AIME), Khan Academy exercises, and algorithmically generated math problems. The problems and their step-by-step solutions are formatted using LaTeX and the Asymptote vector graphics language.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Achieving high accuracy on this dataset with machine learning models could enable students to cheat on their schoolwork, though it would also represent a profound intellectual and practical milestone.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used to benchmark and measure the mathematical problem-solving ability of machine learning models. It is explicitly divided into training and testing splits for fine-tuning and evaluating models.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Upsampling and downsampling were used to balance the sizes of different data sources during pretraining.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data was normalized and formatted consistently to allow for exact match evaluation. This included simplifying fractions, standardizing LaTeX commands for fractions, ordering variables alphabetically, and ignoring spaces.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: To measure the problem-solving ability of machine leaming models, we introduce the MATH dataset... The Mathematics Aptitude Test of Heuristics dataset, abbreviated MATH, has 12;500problems (7;500training and 5;000test).

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: During pretraining, we upsample Khan Academy data by a factor of 5 and we downsample Mathematica by a factor of 2 to account for the large difference in dataset sizes.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: To assess models using exact match, we force the final boxed answers to follow consistent formatting rules. Specifically, probabilities are expressed as simplified fractions. Moreover, matrix entry fractions are encoded with x/y, while all other fractions are consistently encoded with the \frac{x}{y} command.
